title: Trading trumpet for C melody and Lieutenant Mikell's cadet band
summary: He swapped the trumpet for a C melody sax, studied with Rudy Powell and Lieutenant Mikell of the 369th band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: So this friend of mine who played saxophone, Harold Proctor, he advised me that not only would the saxophone be easier to learn, but he would be willing to help me, you

know, and for no fee. No fee involved. So I took the saxophone back, I mean the trumpet back -- and traded it in for a C Melody for the same price, it so happened that I had also been listening to some records by Frankie Trumbauer, and he was playing the C Melody saxophone, and I liked, you know, his sound very much, too.

So I got the C Melody and brought it home, and Harold Hal Proctor taught me for a little while; he taught me how to play the instrument, as far as he felt he could take me, and then he suggested I go to a teacher -- a real teacher -- because Harold Hal Proctor did not read music, as I said. So then I went to this Lieutenant Michael, and I started studying with him. At first, he turned me over to his star pupil, who was very advanced, and his name was Rudy Powell, and then I studied with him for a little while, and then with Lieutenant Michael.

Okay. Does this sound plausible -- this comes from a booklet that was written by George Hoefer in the Jazz Odyssey series, and actually in the third volume called "The Sound of Harlem" and he says in these notes, I believe this is pretty close to a quote, that Eugene Michael -- spelled MIKELL -- was a successor to Jim Europe.
And that he trained what was then the famous 369th Cadet Band.
Yes, I think that's quite right.
And that there were a number of people who later became quite well known, who were under his tutelage in this cadet band, namely Freddie Jenkins, Dean [one J,] Warren, Russell Procope... [To name]
And those you mentioned ... Rudy Powell, and ...
I didn't know that Russell was in the cadet band, but I guess that George Hoefer would probably know, but I don't know that.
